# NPM Improved v1.4.0 — Node Analytics Center

Adds a dedicated **Analytics Center** for measuring traffic handled by the individual NPM Improved node being viewed, while preserving every existing **per-proxy-host Analytics** page and feature.

## Complete node-level view
- A new Analytics Center navigation entry and dedicated interactive dashboard.
- Local-node identification and role, hourly/daily traffic graphs, HTTP status distribution, response/request bytes, latency percentiles, and busiest routes.
- Click-through to existing Host Analytics, filtering by route and response class, and 1-hour / 24-hour / 7-day / 30-day / 90-day windows.
- Request explorer with bounded pagination and sanitized CSV export (up to 10,000 events).
- Traffic breakdowns by hostname, URL path, HTTP method and protocol, device category and upstream status; slowest and most error-prone routes.
- Separate TCP/UDP **stream sessions** section with per-port counts and bytes sent/received. Sessions are not reported as HTTP requests.

## Broader instrumentation
Adds node-local structured Nginx log ingestion for configured HTTP Proxy Hosts, redirects, 404 routes, default and fallback HTTP routes, plus Layer 4 streams. Existing generated configurations activate these logging directives on startup after Nginx syntax validation. Source IDs for different HTTP routing classes are isolated to avoid collisions.

NPMX continues to synchronize configuration, not analytics. Traffic recorded by one node cannot be silently duplicated onto another node.

## Synchronization default
New NPMX node pairings default to **30-second polling**. Existing nodes retain saved intervals, which can be changed in Settings → Instance Synchronization. For dozens of geographically distributed instances, review snapshot transfer volume; event-based WAN fanout and incremental synchronization are future work.

## Retention, accuracy, and privacy
Default raw events retention: 7 days; aggregate rollups: 90 days. No raw IPs, request bodies, query strings, cookies, or secret headers are recorded in the analytics database. Host detail views remain intact. No earlier traffic is invented or backfilled. Reports show whether raw data or historical rollups support the selected range.

## Deployment
Install through the standard NPM Improved release updater on each node, sequentially when NPMX is enabled. All existing proxy routes, certificates and logs are preserved.
